items.question: What is a cross-sectional design?
items.notes: Likely when the student knows the term but cannot explain one-time measurement logic.

items.question: What is a longitudinal design, and how is it different from cross-sectional design?
items.notes: Likely when the student does not clearly distinguish repeated follow-up of the same group from one-time comparison.

items.question: Why can't you read a cross-sectional difference as age change?
items.notes: Likely when the student jumps from age-group comparison to developmental change.

items.question: What is the difference between age effect, cohort effect, and period effect?
items.notes: Likely when the student names the three effects without distinguishing them.

items.question: What exactly is a cohort, and why is it not limited to birth cohort?
items.notes: Likely when the student treats cohort as only a birth-year category.

items.question: Why is it so hard to separate age, cohort, and period effects in one design?
items.notes: Likely when the student remembers the terms but not the methodological problem.

items.question: What are the strengths of cross-sectional design?
items.notes: Likely when the student treats cross-sectional design as only weak or second-best.

items.question: What are the main limits of longitudinal design?
items.notes: Likely when the student praises longitudinal design without mentioning attrition, survivor bias, learning effects, or time and cost burden.

items.question: Why do researchers use mixed or sequential designs such as time-lag or cohort-sequential approaches?
items.notes: Likely when the student gets lost in labels and misses the reason those designs exist.

items.question: What does the long-term longitudinal example show about how aging research evidence is built?
items.notes: Likely when the student remembers the Harvard or Korean example only as an anecdote.

items.question: In the second English paper, how is cohort difference actually being used as an analytic idea?
items.notes: Likely when the student reads the paper but cannot connect it back to the research-method framework.
